sections.heading: Builder Payment Weight Double-Count Fix for Devnet 8
sections.summary: All responding client teams agreed to include the consensus-breaking builder payment weight fix in devnet-8 images without a new spec release.
sections.body:
- [Fix builder payment weight double-count under target equivocation](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5543) was merged end of last week; Barnabas (absent) asked teams to decide on including it in devnet-8.
- The fix is consensus-breaking but hard to trigger in practice.
- Lodestar confirmed they already merged the change and deployed it on the devnet.
  - If other clients do not deploy it, a consensus split could occur if the condition is triggered.
- Lighthouse (Eitan): confirmed they can include it.
- Teku (Stefan): will include it after the call, happy with the change.
- No new Alpha 14 spec release needed; teams will update their images individually, then notify EthPandaOps to update the stable node set.
- Agreement: all client teams to provide updated devnet-8 images incorporating the fix.

sections.heading: Gloas State Transition Compliance Tests
sections.summary: Model-based state transition compliance tests are in progress, with a rough target of mid-September for a full suite; client feedback on existing fork-choice tests is requested.
sections.body:
- Mikhail gave a status update on the compliance testing effort, building on the existing fork-choice compliance test suite.
- Approach: model-based test generation using constraint solvers.
  - Each operation (e.g., process execution payload bid) is modeled with constraints, transpiled to MiniZinc, and solved for all possible input combinations.
  - Solutions are materialized into real Beacon states and operations to create concrete test cases.
- A small subset of tests already exists and is being run with Teku to validate the test generation pipeline and identify issues.
- Test format: reuses existing process-operation test format for all state transition operations and epoch processing; no format changes expected.
- Multi-operation tests planned: tests with multiple operations per block or across block sequences (e.g., builder deposit + builder top-up interactions).
- Rough timeline: full state transition compliance test suite expected by mid-September.
- Mikhail asked clients who have run the fork-choice compliance tests to share feedback on blockers, output issues, or ideas for improvement via Discord.

sections.heading: Epoch Boundary Reorgs in Gloas
sections.summary: Lighthouse already allows epoch boundary reorgs; other clients asked to review the PR to remove the spec-level check, likely to be merged absent objections.
sections.body:
- Justin raised questions about [Allow epoch boundary reorgs in Gloas](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5492) by Potuz, who was not present.
- Background: at ACDT ~84, the team decided to rename the check rather than remove it; Potuz's PR proposes simply removing it.
- Lighthouse (Eitan) confirmed they already allow epoch boundary reorgs on mainnet (no such check in place).
- Nico (Lodestar): if Lighthouse already does this with significant network share, all clients should follow; the proposer is the one most harmed by the reorg since attesters must recompute the epoch transition when they see the block.
- Mikhail: post-Fulu, stable proposer lookahead makes the check unnecessary because an epoch boundary reorg would affect proposer shuffling, which is now fixed.
  - The dependent root for attesters references the previous epoch boundary, not the current one, so removal should be safe.
- Jihoon noted they had previously removed the shuffling check but added it back after feedback about epoch processing concerns; will double-check for problems.
- Nico suggested the PR should specify "after Fulu" rather than "in Gloas" for clarity, though all networks are already on Fulu.
- Action: other client teams asked to review the PR and leave feedback; PR will likely be merged unless a client objects.

sections.heading: Safety Decay Parameter for Historical Block Retention
sections.summary: The safety decay of 100 for historical block retention appears unjustified; Kev will draft an informational EIP proposing 8192 epochs (~1 month) instead of the current ~5 months.
sections.body:
- Kevaundray investigated the MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOCK_REQUESTS constant, which uses a safety decay of 100 (resulting in ~5 months of block retention), because the EL side agreed to copy whatever the CL uses.
  - Some CLs rely on the EL to have the execution payload, so alignment matters.
- Checkpoint syncing uses a safety decay of 10 (~2 weeks); beyond safety decay 33, no additional security benefit exists.
- A safety decay of 100 results in storing roughly 4x more historical blocks than necessary.
- Several clients do not backfill to the full 5 months by default:
  - Links shared for [Prysm](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/blob/462e52404e3965fc0ed4bc1bf7717812d9dd3ef7/cmd/beacon-chain/sync/backfill/flags/flags.go#L12), [Lodestar](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/blob/ec596194e2b909e30e3c6b095fb836427af0c4fb/packages/beacon-node/src/sync/options.ts#L42), and [Grandine](https://github.com/grandinetech/grandine/blob/eaf220e60699cd63d4223ad2481e42fd15f67802/runtime/src/grandine_args.rs#L2027) showing default behavior.
  - If CLs don't backfill 5 months by default, it doesn't make sense for the EL to store 5 months of blocks.
- Mikhail agreed that from a security perspective, a safety decay of 100 doesn't make sense; checkpoint syncing from 5 months ago would be insecure regardless.
  - Mikhail noted the worst case of non-finality should be considered.
  - Kev referenced [EIP-8252](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8252) which implicitly puts the worst case at around a month; however that EIP sets a lower boundary for reorg capability, not a number of blocks to retain.
- Kev's proposal: set retention to 8192 epochs (~36 days), derived by taking the safety decay of 10, doubling it for operational margin, and rounding to a power of two.
  - This would be roughly 2x the blob retention period.
- Action: Kev will draft an informational EIP to codify the proposed change and circulate it for CL team review; if CLs agree, the EL can adopt the reduced constant.

sections.heading: Beacon API and Builder-Specs PRs
sections.summary: Beacon API PR 630 needs final review passes from implementers; Lodestar has a full end-to-end DirectBuilder API implementation, other clients are still in progress.
sections.body:
- Luca asked about a target date for merging Beacon API changes in [PR 630](https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/630).
- Nico (Lodestar): gave multiple review passes over the weekend; the PR has been reworked ~5 times and is close to mergeable, but needs final approvals from other implementers.
- Three related PRs need implementer approvals to merge: the Beacon API PR (630), a builder-specs PR, and [keymanager-APIs PR 88](https://github.com/ethereum/keymanager-APIs/pull/88#discussion_r3789665268).
  - Jason noted PR 88 has one open question about whether the GET endpoint should return the pub key for consistency.
  - James (Prysm): no strong opinions; historical gRPC restrictions no longer apply; deferred to Jason.
  - Decision: keep as is (include the pub key).
- DirectBuilder API implementation status:
  - Lodestar (Nico): fully implemented end-to-end based on Jason's latest spec; found and resolved some outdated Builder API URLs.
  - Prysm (James): KeyManager 88 implemented, but not Beacon API 630 end-to-end yet. Mark did a full implementation but it hasn't been reviewed/merged.
  - Lighthouse (Eitan): Mark did a full implementation, pending review and merge.
  - Teku (Stefan): still in progress, hoping to have something this week.
- Testing on devnet-8:
  - Nico plans to have DirectBuilder working before the fork to test the transition at the fork boundary.
  - Ideally want a builder bid at Gloas slot 0, though discovery of assigned builder index at fork boundary may make slot 0 challenging.
  - Unclear if any builder is currently exposing an API for testing on devnet.
- Nico asked for approval on the builder-specs and Beacon API PRs; needs one more day of review on the Lodestar implementation before feeling fully comfortable.
